questions.q: In the audit, what did facilities_admin's Contains Roles field actually show?
options: It contained none — its read access was granted through separate, duplicated ACL grants instead of inheriting from facilities_viewer
It contained facilities_viewer, exactly as its name implied
It contained facilities_super_admin
It had no ACL grants of any kind
questions.explain: The audit found facilities_admin duplicated facilities_viewer's read access with its own independent ACL grants rather than containing it — two paths to the same permission.

questions.q: Why was facilities_super_admin flagged during the audit, beyond its ACL content?
options: Because it granted no permissions at all
Because it was missing from the sys_user_role table entirely
Because the one person it was built for had left the company fourteen months earlier, and nobody had revoked or re-evaluated the role since
Because it granted fewer permissions than facilities_viewer
questions.explain: The role sat unassigned and unreviewed for over a year after its original purpose ended — a dormant role nobody had retired.

questions.q: What did the redesign do with facilities_viewer's read access in the new two-role hierarchy?
options: It was deleted entirely with no replacement
It was merged directly into facilities_super_admin
It stayed exactly as it was, unchanged
It became facilities_user, the single source of read access that facilities_admin now contains instead of duplicating
questions.explain: facilities_user became the base role holding read access once; facilities_admin was rebuilt to contain it instead of granting duplicate read ACLs.

questions.q: Why was facilities_super_admin retired outright rather than folded into the redesigned hierarchy?
options: Because ServiceNow does not allow more than two custom roles per department
Because its one real use case had ended over a year earlier and no one currently needed its delete permission
Because it was technically impossible to redesign a role with a Contains Roles field
Because facilities_admin could never grant delete permissions under any circumstances
questions.explain: Retiring a role whose need has genuinely expired is as important as designing new roles narrowly — a dormant role is still part of what must be audited.

questions.q: What made facilities_admin's original design a quiet form of role sprawl, even though no individual ACL in it was wrong?
options: It granted permissions on the wrong table entirely
It was assigned to too many users
It granted the correct permissions through a redundant, independent path instead of inheriting from the role that already granted them, adding hard-to-audit duplication to the hierarchy
It lacked any read access whatsoever
questions.explain: Sprawl isn't only about wrong permissions — duplicating a correct grant through a separate, uncontained path still adds complexity that makes the whole hierarchy harder to audit.
